title: The EU’s Incredible Shrinking Banking Sector
gist: A teaser noting that a quarter-century ago each of the five largest EU banks was worth more than the biggest US bank, whereas today JPMorganChase alone exceeds the combined market capitalization of the EU's top five — a reversal the author frames as a policy problem for Europe.

insights.claim: At the start of the millennium each of the five biggest European Union banks had a larger market capitalization than the largest US bank; today JPMorganChase alone is worth more than the top five EU banks combined.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: A complete inversion of transatlantic banking scale in 25 years — the structural case for the persistent US-over-Europe financials valuation gap.
insights.quote: Now the market capitalization of the biggest US bank, JPMorganChase, is higher than that of the top five EU banks combined.

insights.claim: The EU's top five banks by market capitalization are presumed to include France's BNP Paribas, Germany's Deutsche Bank, and Spain's Santander, though EU disclosures do not name them.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific names carrying Europe's banking-scale deficit — the likely beneficiaries of any EU consolidation or capital-markets-union push.
insights.quote: The EU is coy about names, but we can presume that the EU banks include France’s BNP Paribas, Germany’s Deutsche Bank, and Spain’s Santander
insights.locator: The EU is coy about names

insights.claim: The collapse in relative valuation of European banks is treated as a policy failure that European policymakers are expected to address rather than as a neutral market outcome.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Frames EU banking-sector reform as a live political agenda item — a catalyst path for European financials if consolidation or regulatory relief follows.
insights.quote: how can European policymakers address this dramatic reversal?
